title: 2015 AMC 10A 21
statement: Tetrahedron \(ABCD\) has \(AB=5,\) \(AC=3,\) \(BC=4,\) \(BD=4,\) \(AD=3,\) and \(CD=\tfrac{12}5\sqrt2.\) What is the volume of the tetrahedron?

solutions.text:
We claim that the planes \(ABC\) and \(ABD\) are perpendicular to each other.

We can show this by dropping the perpendiculars from \(C\) and \(D\) to \(AB\).

Since \(AC = AD\) and \(BC = BD,\) we have that the feet of these altitudes will coincide at point \(P.\)

Then we have that \[ CP = DP = \dfrac{3 \cdot 4}{5} = \dfrac{12}{5}. \] We also have \(CD = CP\sqrt{2},\) so \(\triangle CPD\) is an isosceles right triangle and \(CP\perp DP.\)

Since \(CP\perp AB\) and \(CP\perp DP\), the segment \(CP\) is perpendicular to the plane \(ABD\). Finally, the volume of the tetrahedron is \[ \dfrac{1}{3}[ABD] \cdot CP = \dfrac{6}{3} \cdot \dfrac{12}{5} = \dfrac{24}{5}. \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Put the two \(3\)-\(4\)-\(5\) triangles on a common base \(AB\)
